about.title: About
about.body: music-platform is a catalog and community for logging and reviewing the music you've already listened to — a Letterboxd for music. It is not a player or an audio source: it builds on MusicBrainz's open data and on what its own community contributes.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.body: This is where the platform's terms of use will live: what you may post, who owns the content you upload, and when an account may be suspended.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.body: This is where we'll set out what personal data is collected, on what legal basis, how long it is kept, and how to exercise your rights over it.
privacy.intro: This is the part of the policy that already describes what the application does today with your account and data. The rest of the document is being prepared.

personal.title: Optional personal details on your profile
personal.body: On your profile you can add, if you want, your country, your city or region, your pronouns, a bio, your time zone and, if you turn it on, your local time. Everything is optional, starts empty and today is used only to show it on your profile.
personal.body2: Who sees it: on a public profile, anyone; on a private profile, only you and the people who follow you with an approved request. The bio, links and counters follow the usual rule and are shown on the card of a private profile.
personal.body3: We never ask for it when you sign up. You can change or clear it whenever you want from Settings → Profile, and it is deleted with your account when you delete it. We do not collect your birth date, your gender or your legal name in separate fields: the only name is the “Display name”, which can be a nickname.

deactivate.title: Deactivating your account
deactivate.body: From Settings → Account and security you can deactivate your account to take a break. Your profile stops being visible to other people: it does not appear in search, followers, following, the feed, community activity or lists, and nobody can follow or block you. We sign you out everywhere. You must confirm your identity to do it.
deactivate.body2: Deactivating deletes nothing: we keep your ratings, reviews, comments, lists, favorites, diary and follows. Your ratings still count in averages, and your reviews and comments stay visible with the author shown as “Deactivated account”, without your username, your name or a link to your profile.

reactivate.title: Reactivating your account
reactivate.body: Signing in, with your password or with Google, reactivates your account immediately and everything is visible again as it was. There is no extra confirmation step: if you do not want your profile to be visible again, do not sign in.

delete.title: Deleting your account
delete.body: Also from Account and security you can delete your account. We delete the account and everything you created: profile, links and prompts, ratings, reviews, comments, lists, favorites, diary, collection, follows, blocks, reports you filed and sessions. Other people’s data is not affected.
delete.body2: Deleting is immediate and irreversible: there is currently no grace period. To confirm, we ask you to type your username and confirm your identity. If you only want a break, deactivate the account.

export.title: Downloading your data
export.body: In the same place you can download a JSON file with your data: account, profile, library (including private diary notes), activity, lists and network. For people who follow you or that you follow, only the public username is included. The file never includes your password, tokens or sessions. One download per minute is allowed.

limits.title: What cannot be deleted today
limits.body: An account with moderation or editorial history cannot be deleted, because we keep the record of those actions (who did them and when). It can be deactivated instead. A deactivated account keeps its data until you reactivate or delete it.

pending.title: To be defined before the public launch
pending.body: These points are not settled yet and this policy does not promise them:
items: Recovery period: we are considering having deletion leave the account deactivated and recoverable for 14 to 30 days before the final purge, to cover mistakes or unauthorized access. Today deletion is immediate.
Backups and technical logs: define how long until the data of a deleted account disappears from them.
Deactivated accounts: define how long they are kept without activity (today, no limit).
Moderation records: anonymize the person in those records so accounts with history can be deleted, instead of blocking it.
Data we must keep because of a legal obligation (fraud, legal requests): define which, for how long and isolated from the rest.
Right to erasure: confirm the deadlines and legal basis for each jurisdiction (for example, GDPR Art. 17 requires erasure without undue delay, generally within one month).
Reactivation: today signing in is enough, with no confirmation or notice. Revisit if there are complaints about unintended reactivations.
Minimum age: set in the Terms of service the minimum age to use the platform. Today age is neither asked nor verified.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.body: Today the app only uses a strictly necessary session cookie to keep you signed in; it needs no consent. If analytics or other cookies are added later, they'll be explained here and your consent will be requested.

guidelines.title: Community Guidelines
guidelines.body: This is where we'll describe what's expected of reviews, comments and lists, and what content the platform moderates.
